turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, Hale. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and when?
You need "an answer today." So do I, and I asked first. Was Owen heard before that zero went into the gradebook, yes or no?
Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript.

Owen "admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM" or it goes on his transcript; I'm writing that down word for word. Your own procedure, section 4.4, gives a first concern a supervised reassessment and puts nothing in the record, so on what basis are you skipping it? Answer that, or my next stop is the principal's office.
Those are the only two options. Pick one.

"The only two options." Neither, Hale, because Owen has nothing to admit and your own policy gives a third. Unless you have something with a date on it that you haven't shown me, I'm walking upstairs to the principal right now.
